one-line thesis: The strongest opening quarter in MPS's history, and the *shape* is the story: **revenue +20.4%, EBITDA +53.0%, headcount up less than 3%** — margin expanded to **34.3% from 27.0%** with growth converting into margin rather than consuming it, and **all three segments expanded margin simultaneously**. Two structural claims explain it and both are now testable: **(a)** revenue is shifting from being paid for *effort* to being paid for *outcomes* — already **25% of revenue is outcome-based partnerships and 45% recurring**; **(b)** AI is deflationary for content *generation* but inflationary for content *verification*, and MPS sits deliberately at *"the layer where AI cannot afford to be wrong."* Guidance was reaffirmed and hardened — **>₹300cr FY27 EBITDA framed explicitly as a floor**, plus a first clear articulation of **FY28: ~₹1,500cr revenue and ~₹450cr EBITDA**. The one genuine soft spot, which an analyst pressed and management conceded without deflection: **ex-Unbound organic growth is only early-teens**, and corporate learning is growing 6–7% into a 12–13% market.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **FY27 EBITDA: "comfortably cross ₹300 crores"** — reaffirmed and explicitly reframed: *"read that number the way we read it internally, as a floor rather than a ceiling"* and *"a floor we intend to clear, not a target we hope to reach."* Built bottom-up from segment operating plans at an **unchanged planning [FX] rate**; implies a **~21% three-year EBITDA CAGR FY24→FY27**. Q1 is **ahead of a straight-line path**, and H2 has historically outrun H1.
- **FY28: ~₹1,500cr revenue and ~₹450cr EBITDA** — the CEO corrected an analyst who thought ₹1,500cr was an FY27 target: *"The INR 1,500 crores is for FY'28 next year, and that probably will translate to more like INR 450 crores EBITDA."*
- **Rule of 50 for full-year FY27** — *"Rule of 50 is a mark we are hopeful of clearing for the full year"*, with an explicit refusal to promise it every quarter (*"the phasing of our business does not work that neatly"*). Q1 cleared it (20% growth + 34% margin).
- **Peer review: #2 → #1 provider in the industry by volume by end of this calendar/financial year** — *"We are now the second largest peer-review provider in the industry by volume, and we aim to be the first by the end of this year."* A hard, externally checkable market-position commitment.
- **Corporate Learning steady state: ~30% EBITDA margin and ~12% organic growth** (currently 25.3% and 6.9%); near-term focus is to **hold the Q1 exit margin as the run-rate**, make AI-led delivery the dominant mix, and **complete integration of legacy entities into one unified Liberate Global brand**.
- **Unbound Medicine:** current run-rate **~$800k/month** at **18–20% margins**; target is to climb to **Rule of 40 (EBITDA margin mid-to-late 20s)** and eventually **Rule of 50**. Synergy timelines deliberately **not committed** until the renewal cycle is understood.
- **Organic growth ambition:** outperform every end-market — research market ~8–9% (MPS ~15%), education market ~15% (MPS higher), **corporate market 12–13% vs MPS 6–7%, the acknowledged catch-up**. CEO accepted the analyst's challenge to target **late-teens organic growth**.
- **M&A: no equity issuance.** *"I don't see an equity play here... this is a cash-plus-debt financing story."* Deal size **₹300–500cr** comfortably fundable from **₹138cr cash + ₹15–18cr/month accruals + ~₹200cr of debt**. Screening filters: **≥$15mn revenue**, **≥10% three-year revenue CAGR**, **current EBITDA 5–15%** (MPS's value-add is taking it to ~30%), Education-weighted, science/high-stakes domains where **AI is a tailwind not a subtractor**.
- **Accessibility line: a large journals rollout later this year.**
- **Long-range framing:** *"while we discussed Vision 2027 and FY'28, we are building for 2032."*
order book & pipeline: No order-book metric (subscription + project mix), but the forward indicators given are specific: **multi-year platform contracts** (HighWire, DigiCore Pro, THINK365) described as the stickiest revenue and *"not easily replaced"*; **multi-year, multi-product programs** with several of the largest US K-12 and higher-education knowledge organisations, moved out of pilot; **a large journals accessibility rollout later this year**; **multiple Corporate Learning enterprise engagements approaching the $1mn mark** plus a healthy new-logo pipeline; and **the largest publishers in the world entrusting MPS with more of their submission workflow, including their most sensitive portfolios**. Unbound adds **recurring, high-renewal institutional subscriptions** — the most predictable forward revenue MPS has ever had.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Research Solutions (55% of revenue, 45.1% margin).** Run as a layered product stack rather than a services book: **(1) trust & integrity** — DigiCore live in client delivery at top-tier knowledge organisations, with Research Integrity Check on top detecting **paper mills, identity fraud and image manipulation**; **(2) production** — AI composition/quality workflows live in delivery, producing one-touch workflows, **automated alt-text**, and AI quality checks catching errors before proof; **(3) platform** — HighWire, DigiCore Pro, THINK365 as hosting/publishing backbone on multi-year contracts; underneath, **MPS Labs** compounds across all segments at near-zero marginal cost.
- **AJE (author solutions) — shrinking by design.** Revenue deliberately smaller as the consumer base finds its level, but *"far more profitable and far higher in quality than the inflated base we carried two years ago."* **Pruning is declared over.** First new service in more than two years — **Pre-Submission Peer Review, launched April 2026** — with demand *"well ahead of what we planned."* Entire US cost base offshored to India by end-Q4 FY26, and **NPS rose through the transition**.
- **Pre-acceptance peer review & journal editorial office — the offence.** One of the fastest-growing lines; scaled off the AJE acquisition; **#2 by volume, targeting #1 by end of year**; handled by a small team only because of homegrown AI tooling.
- **Education Solutions (+42.2%).** Beyond Unbound, three organic drivers: AI-enabled content/production deepening with the largest US K-12 and higher-ed organisations (pilots → multi-year multi-product); the **accessibility** line (AI-produced accessible learning media, high-margin, building toward a large journals rollout); and a genuinely new lane — **clients paying MPS to review and quality-check AI-generated instructional content**, *"a service that did not exist for us a year ago."*
- **Unbound Medicine — first full quarter, thesis validated.** ~**$800k/month** revenue at **18–20% margin**, delivered by a **35-person team doing ~$9mn of revenue**. Brings recurring high-renewal subscriptions across medical/nursing schools, hospitals and academic libraries — **lowering customer concentration without any anchor relationship billing less**. Capability brought in: **"Unbound Intelligence"**, a knowledge-engineering layer that answers clinician questions from **paywalled, peer-reviewed publisher content rather than the open web** — i.e. AI products that structurally cannot hallucinate.
- **Corporate Learning / Liberate Global (+6.9% revenue, +60.7% EBITDA).** Repositioned *"from learning creation to enterprise capability enablement"* — enhancing clients' existing LMS/LXP/SharePoint with AI, simulations and immersive experiences, reusable across business units and geographies. Headcount down ~33% in three parts: **structural redundancy (largest, one-time)**, **fixed→variable gig/associate capacity**, and **AI productivity (smallest but growing)**. Senior instructional-design and client-facing benches were **untouched**; margin expanded **without any rise in rework or client escalations**.

- **Liberate × Unbound cross-sell** — discovered post-acquisition on a US roadshow: Unbound's medical/nursing platform is content-rich but *"everything is more physical and tactical even now... there is little around learning by doing."* Liberate's immersive/simulation capability layers on top of Unbound's renewal base — described as *"a huge cross-selling opportunity"* and *"more of a top-up"* on recurring revenue.
- **Pricing power at Unbound** — flagged as the CEO's third surprise learning: *"every renewal with a customer, whether it's a 10-year-old customer or a 3-year-old customer, there is a price increase. Every year within a term of a contract, there is a price increase."* MPS now believes there are *"tremendous areas where there's disproportionate value being created by MPS, and there's potential opportunity to increase prices"* across its own portfolio.
- **AI-content QC as a new revenue line** in Education.
- **M&A pipeline** — active, Education-weighted, with cybersecurity named alongside medicine/nursing as an example of the high-stakes domains being screened.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **The verification control point.** *"The bottleneck in research today is no longer generating content; it is verifying it. That is precisely the control point we occupy."* And the inversion of the commoditisation fear: *"As models get stronger, the constraint moves away from generating content and toward verifying it, toward domain context, toward the last mile inside a real workflow. That last mile is exactly where MPS sits, and it is a tailwind for us, not a threat."*
- **Walled-garden data as the anti-hallucination moat.** Unbound Intelligence scrapes **paywalled, peer-reviewed publisher content and MPS's own assets**, not the open web: *"The Unbound evidence tool or chat cannot get it wrong because it's not coming from someone's opinion. It's coming from science... if the same nurse went to ChatGPT, there's no guarantee whether ChatGPT would scrape the web, what it would scrape."* The moat is **access rights**, not model quality.
- **Switching costs in the platform layer:** HighWire, DigiCore Pro and THINK365 run *"mission-critical workflows and are not easily replaced"* on multi-year contracts.
- **Trust as a barrier in peer review:** the largest publishers handing over *"some of their most sensitive portfolios, which is not a decision anyone makes lightly."*
- **Measured outcome superiority:** MPS's controlled work shows a **manuscript acceptance rate of ~52% against an industry baseline near 32%** — the quantified basis for charging for outcomes rather than hours.
- **Shared R&D compounding:** MPS Labs' work *"compounds across every segment at very little marginal cost. That is not a feature. It is a structural moat."*
- **Evidence the cuts were structural, not capability-destroying:** AJE fully offshored **and NPS went up** — *"I've never seen a transition like this where quality improves."*
margins & cost dynamics:
Margin expanded **730bps** on **<3% headcount growth** — the cleanest operating-leverage quarter in the company's history, and it held in **all three segments simultaneously**. Mechanics:
- **Research (45.1%):** AI moved *"from pilot to core delivery"*, allowing materially more work on a held cost line.
- **Education (35.1%):** Unbound mix plus AI-enabled production; accessibility is explicitly high-margin.
- **Corporate Learning (16.9% → 25.3%):** *"we rebuilt the cost base rather than chasing volumes"* — ~33% lower headcount, gig/variable capacity, and AI-enabled authoring. Steady state guided at **~30%**.
- **The offsetting cost swing:** AJE offshoring (all US roles to India by end-Q4 FY26) absorbed both annual increments and Unbound's headcount addition. **This offset is now spent** — future margin must come from mix and AI, not from repeating the arbitrage.
- **FX:** guidance is built at an **unchanged planning rate**. Corporate Learning has **less North America exposure** than Research/Education, so less dollar benefit there.
- **Structural margin driver:** outcome-based revenue *"carries better economics than effort, because the value sits in the result rather than the input"* — the CEO's explicit attribution for why 20% revenue growth produced 53% EBITDA growth.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No physical capex programme — expansion is via **M&A and AI/engineering R&D (MPS Labs)**. Commitments to watch: **completing the consolidation of legacy corporate-learning entities into one Liberate Global brand**; the **large journals accessibility rollout later this year**; **Unbound synergy timelines deliberately withheld** until the renewal cycle is learned (a sensible discipline, but also an unbounded commitment); and an **active acquisition pipeline** gated on finding *"a motivated seller"* — the CEO's own admission that timing is not in his control.
capital allocation:
The most explicit capital-allocation framework MPS has articulated:
- **Order of funding:** cash accruals (**₹138cr on hand, ₹15–18cr/month generated**) → debt (*"assume PAT of INR 200 crores... corresponding to that, debt of INR 200 crores is comfortable"*) → **equity only as a never-say-never last resort**. A shareholder explicitly asked him not to dilute; he agreed.
- **Deal capacity: ₹300–500cr**, fundable without equity.
- **Screening filters:** ≥$15mn revenue (Unbound was a deliberate exception *"simply because of how good the asset was"*), ≥10% three-year revenue CAGR, EBITDA 5–15% on entry (MPS takes it to ~30% and *"unlocks the rule of 40 for each of these assets"*), Education-weighted, science/high-stakes domain.
- **Strategy has explicitly pivoted away from distressed assets.** The candid reasoning: distressed deals were *"highly accretive financially — look at our ROCE... north of 30%, sometimes even north of 50%"* **but** *"distracts you from the very organic growth you're pointing us towards because the entire management team is rescuing a new asset every year."*
- **Culture as a veto:** they **walked away at an advanced stage** from an attractive Education asset over *"shortcuts the management team had taken with some of the customers"* — a rare, specific disclosure of a deal killed on non-financial grounds.
- **Retention mechanics:** target teams identified during diligence, retained via stock options and **larger roles on the MPS platform**.
risks & watch-items:
1. **Organic growth is the acknowledged weak link.** Strip Unbound and group growth is **early-teens**; **Corporate Learning grows 6–7% into a 12–13% market**. The CEO accepted the challenge to reach late-teens but committed to no number or date.
2. **The AJE-offshoring cost offset is non-repeating.** It masked increments and Unbound headcount this quarter; from here, margin gains must come from mix and AI alone.
3. **Corporate Learning's margin jump is restructuring-led** (~33% headcount cut, largely a *"one-time reset"*). Holding 25.3% and progressing to 30% now requires the AI/immersive mix shift to actually land.
4. **Client count fell QoQ (906 → 841)** — explained entirely as AJE pruning, but worth verifying it stops now that management says *"the pruning is behind us."*
5. **Management churn** — an analyst opened by asking what is driving *"exits and replacements"* over the last year. The CEO's answer was candid but not reassuring: *"as the talent machine expands in a quick span of time, sometimes you make mistakes."* Education's business head was on his first MPS earnings call.
6. **Unbound is 18–20% margin against a 34% group margin** — near-term it is **dilutive to group margin** even as it is accretive to quality of revenue. The path to Rule of 40 is a target, not a plan.
7. **M&A dependency:** the FY28 ₹1,500cr/₹450cr target is difficult on early-teens organic growth alone, and deal timing is gated on *"a motivated seller"* — outside management's control.
8. **AJE reset must actually be over.** It has depressed reported Research and group growth for two years; a further leg down would undercut the *"grow on value rather than volume"* claim.
9. **Peer-review #1-by-year-end is a public, binary commitment** on a metric MPS does not control alone.
10. **Concentration in Research (55% of revenue at 45.1% margin)** — group margin is highly sensitive to any single-segment reversal.
11. **FX:** guidance assumes an unchanged planning rate; a sharp rupee appreciation would pressure a largely North-America-billed book.
management quality / tone: Among the best-run calls in the batch. Structural choices that signal confidence: **six executives on the call**, with the two halves of Research narrated by the two people who actually run them and the Education head making his debut — *"Hearing about the business directly from the people building it is exactly how I want these calls to feel."* Substantively, management **quantified its own dilutions** (ex-AJE revenue and margin given unprompted), **corrected an analyst's misreading of the ₹1,500cr target** rather than letting a flattering error stand, **explicitly declined to promise Rule of 50 every quarter** (*"we are a conservative lot here at MPS when it comes to star gazing"*), **refused to commit Unbound synergy timelines** until the renewal cycle is understood, **conceded the organic-growth shortfall** when pushed (*"thank you for pushing us... The quarter that you see is in the rear-view mirror"*), and **disclosed a walked-away acquisition and its ethical reason**. The closing remarks summarised the analysts' three challenges back at them — including the demand for late-teens organic growth — which is unusual and credible. The only real gap: **no direct answer on why senior managers have been exiting**, beyond a general "the talent machine sometimes gets it wrong."
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The commoditisation argument is inverted, and coherently.** Most knowledge-services companies are AI-threatened because they sell generation. MPS argues that stronger models **increase** the value of verification, domain context and the workflow last mile. Whether or not it proves right, it is the correct axis on which to judge the business.
- **The moat is content *access rights*, not AI capability.** Unbound Intelligence's advantage is that it reads **behind publisher paywalls** — something no general model can replicate regardless of parameter count.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Research Solutions (55% of revenue, 45.1% margin).** Run as a layered product stack rather than a services book: **(1) trust & integrity** — DigiCore live in client delivery at top-tier knowledge organisations, with Research Integrity Check on top detecting **paper mills, identity fraud and image manipulation**; **(2) production** — AI composition/quality workflows live in delivery, producing one-touch workflows, **automated alt-text**, and AI quality checks catching errors before proof; **(3) platform** — HighWire, DigiCore Pro, THINK365 as hosting/publishing backbone on multi-year contracts; underneath, **MPS Labs** compounds across all segments at near-zero marginal cost.
- **AJE (author solutions) — shrinking by design.** Revenue deliberately smaller as the consumer base finds its level, but *"far more profitable and far higher in quality than the inflated base we carried two years ago."* **Pruning is declared over.** First new service in more than two years — **Pre-Submission Peer Review, launched April 2026** — with demand *"well ahead of what we planned."* Entire US cost base offshored to India by end-Q4 FY26, and **NPS rose through the transition**.
- **Pre-acceptance peer review & journal editorial office — the offence.** One of the fastest-growing lines; scaled off the AJE acquisition; **#2 by volume, targeting #1 by end of year**; handled by a small team only because of homegrown AI tooling.
- **Education Solutions (+42.2%).** Beyond Unbound, three organic drivers: AI-enabled content/production deepening with the largest US K-12 and higher-ed organisations (pilots → multi-year multi-product); the **accessibility** line (AI-produced accessible learning media, high-margin, building toward a large journals rollout); and a genuinely new lane — **clients paying MPS to review and quality-check AI-generated instructional content**, *"a service that did not exist for us a year ago."*
- **Unbound Medicine — first full quarter, thesis validated.** ~**$800k/month** revenue at **18–20% margin**, delivered by a **35-person team doing ~$9mn of revenue**. Brings recurring high-renewal subscriptions across medical/nursing schools, hospitals and academic libraries — **lowering customer concentration without any anchor relationship billing less**. Capability brought in: **"Unbound Intelligence"**, a knowledge-engineering layer that answers clinician questions from **paywalled, peer-reviewed publisher content rather than the open web** — i.e. AI products that structurally cannot hallucinate.
- **Corporate Learning / Liberate Global (+6.9% revenue, +60.7% EBITDA).** Repositioned *"from learning creation to enterprise capability enablement"* — enhancing clients' existing LMS/LXP/SharePoint with AI, simulations and immersive experiences, reusable across business units and geographies. Headcount down ~33% in three parts: **structural redundancy (largest, one-time)**, **fixed→variable gig/associate capacity**, and **AI productivity (smallest but growing)**. Senior instructional-design and client-facing benches were **untouched**; margin expanded **without any rise in rework or client escalations**.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 EBITDA: "comfortably cross ₹300 crores"** — reaffirmed and explicitly reframed: *"read that number the way we read it internally, as a floor rather than a ceiling"* and *"a floor we intend to clear, not a target we hope to reach."* Built bottom-up from segment operating plans at an **unchanged planning [FX] rate**; implies a **~21% three-year EBITDA CAGR FY24→FY27**. Q1 is **ahead of a straight-line path**, and H2 has historically outrun H1.
- **FY28: ~₹1,500cr revenue and ~₹450cr EBITDA** — the CEO corrected an analyst who thought ₹1,500cr was an FY27 target: *"The INR 1,500 crores is for FY'28 next year, and that probably will translate to more like INR 450 crores EBITDA."*
- **Rule of 50 for full-year FY27** — *"Rule of 50 is a mark we are hopeful of clearing for the full year"*, with an explicit refusal to promise it every quarter (*"the phasing of our business does not work that neatly"*). Q1 cleared it (20% growth + 34% margin).
- **Peer review: #2 → #1 provider in the industry by volume by end of this calendar/financial year** — *"We are now the second largest peer-review provider in the industry by volume, and we aim to be the first by the end of this year."* A hard, externally checkable market-position commitment.
- **Corporate Learning steady state: ~30% EBITDA margin and ~12% organic growth** (currently 25.3% and 6.9%); near-term focus is to **hold the Q1 exit margin as the run-rate**, make AI-led delivery the dominant mix, and **complete integration of legacy entities into one unified Liberate Global brand**.
- **Unbound Medicine:** current run-rate **~$800k/month** at **18–20% margins**; target is to climb to **Rule of 40 (EBITDA margin mid-to-late 20s)** and eventually **Rule of 50**. Synergy timelines deliberately **not committed** until the renewal cycle is understood.
- **Organic growth ambition:** outperform every end-market — research market ~8–9% (MPS ~15%), education market ~15% (MPS higher), **corporate market 12–13% vs MPS 6–7%, the acknowledged catch-up**. CEO accepted the analyst's challenge to target **late-teens organic growth**.
- **M&A: no equity issuance.** *"I don't see an equity play here... this is a cash-plus-debt financing story."* Deal size **₹300–500cr** comfortably fundable from **₹138cr cash + ₹15–18cr/month accruals + ~₹200cr of debt**. Screening filters: **≥$15mn revenue**, **≥10% three-year revenue CAGR**, **current EBITDA 5–15%** (MPS's value-add is taking it to ~30%), Education-weighted, science/high-stakes domains where **AI is a tailwind not a subtractor**.
- **Accessibility line: a large journals rollout later this year.**
- **Long-range framing:** *"while we discussed Vision 2027 and FY'28, we are building for 2032."*

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Outcome-based pricing expansion** — already **25% of revenue**; premium author tiers, shared AI productivity gains, and expansion into **China**, where partnerships have already been signed.
- **Liberate × Unbound cross-sell** — discovered post-acquisition on a US roadshow: Unbound's medical/nursing platform is content-rich but *"everything is more physical and tactical even now... there is little around learning by doing."* Liberate's immersive/simulation capability layers on top of Unbound's renewal base — described as *"a huge cross-selling opportunity"* and *"more of a top-up"* on recurring revenue.
- **Pricing power at Unbound** — flagged as the CEO's third surprise learning: *"every renewal with a customer, whether it's a 10-year-old customer or a 3-year-old customer, there is a price increase. Every year within a term of a contract, there is a price increase."* MPS now believes there are *"tremendous areas where there's disproportionate value being created by MPS, and there's potential opportunity to increase prices"* across its own portfolio.
- **AI-content QC as a new revenue line** in Education.
- **M&A pipeline** — active, Education-weighted, with cybersecurity named alongside medicine/nursing as an example of the high-stakes domains being screened.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Artificial intelligence has made content almost free to produce while making trusted knowledge harder to find; this widening gap between generated content and verified knowledge is management's core demand driver
- AI is shifting from generative to agentic, automating editorial, peer-review, production and learning workflows, which management frames as increasing demand for MPS' services
- Research integrity is described as a defining industry challenge, with more than 14,000 retraction notices issued in 2023 and 'paper mills' industrialising fraud, raising the value of trusted screening
- Open science mandates such as Plan S are reshaping publishing economics
- Customers across every segment are consolidating spend onto scaled, full-service partners that reduce vendor complexity, which management positions MPS to capture
- Education solutions market valued at approximately USD 416 billion in 2025, projected to reach roughly USD 878 billion by 2031, driven by digital, personalised and lifelong learning
- Corporate e-learning market valued at approximately USD 353 billion in 2025, projected to approach USD 874 billion by 2030 as workforces reskill
- Research and scholarly services expanding with global research output (about 3.5 million science and engineering articles in 2024) and associated compliance demands
- Healthcare knowledge management flagged as a fast-growing adjacency MPS entered in FY26 through Unbound Medicine, at the intersection of clinical content and AI
- Segment mix commentary: Research Solutions delivered 'the recovery', Education Solutions delivered 'the scale' (strongest portfolio growth), and Corporate Learning delivered 'the turn' (return to growth in Q4FY26)
- Headline consolidated revenue growth of 5.71% understates the underlying operating performance because a lower-quality book of business was deliberately shrunk; excluding the AJE and Unbound acquisitions the rest of the business grew by approximately 13.3%
- Margin expansion (170 bps) attributed to a cost reset taking hold, with group manpower cost down even as Unbound entered the base and senior hiring continued
- Research Solutions: Journals took on substantial new business from leading global publishers while building capacity with discipline
- Research Solutions: Scholarly Books secured a major multi-year commitment for 900 titles
- Research Solutions: Platforms continued migrating publishers onto the HighWire stack, strengthening long-term customer relationships
- Research Solutions segment closed FY26 with strong margin recovery and 'a fuller pipeline than it began with'
- Corporate Learning: MPS Interactive Systems led the turnaround on a stronger order book; Liberate Learning rebuilt its commercial pipeline after becoming wholly owned

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
Margin expanded **730bps** on **<3% headcount growth** — the cleanest operating-leverage quarter in the company's history, and it held in **all three segments simultaneously**. Mechanics:
- **Research (45.1%):** AI moved *"from pilot to core delivery"*, allowing materially more work on a held cost line.
- **Education (35.1%):** Unbound mix plus AI-enabled production; accessibility is explicitly high-margin.
- **Corporate Learning (16.9% → 25.3%):** *"we rebuilt the cost base rather than chasing volumes"* — ~33% lower headcount, gig/variable capacity, and AI-enabled authoring. Steady state guided at **~30%**.
- **The offsetting cost swing:** AJE offshoring (all US roles to India by end-Q4 FY26) absorbed both annual increments and Unbound's headcount addition. **This offset is now spent** — future margin must come from mix and AI, not from repeating the arbitrage.
- **FX:** guidance is built at an **unchanged planning rate**. Corporate Learning has **less North America exposure** than Research/Education, so less dollar benefit there.
- **Structural margin driver:** outcome-based revenue *"carries better economics than effort, because the value sits in the result rather than the input"* — the CEO's explicit attribution for why 20% revenue growth produced 53% EBITDA growth.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
The most explicit capital-allocation framework MPS has articulated:
- **Order of funding:** cash accruals (**₹138cr on hand, ₹15–18cr/month generated**) → debt (*"assume PAT of INR 200 crores... corresponding to that, debt of INR 200 crores is comfortable"*) → **equity only as a never-say-never last resort**. A shareholder explicitly asked him not to dilute; he agreed.
- **Deal capacity: ₹300–500cr**, fundable without equity.
- **Screening filters:** ≥$15mn revenue (Unbound was a deliberate exception *"simply because of how good the asset was"*), ≥10% three-year revenue CAGR, EBITDA 5–15% on entry (MPS takes it to ~30% and *"unlocks the rule of 40 for each of these assets"*), Education-weighted, science/high-stakes domain.
- **Strategy has explicitly pivoted away from distressed assets.** The candid reasoning: distressed deals were *"highly accretive financially — look at our ROCE... north of 30%, sometimes even north of 50%"* **but** *"distracts you from the very organic growth you're pointing us towards because the entire management team is rescuing a new asset every year."*
- **Culture as a veto:** they **walked away at an advanced stage** from an attractive Education asset over *"shortcuts the management team had taken with some of the customers"* — a rare, specific disclosure of a deal killed on non-financial grounds.
- **Retention mechanics:** target teams identified during diligence, retained via stock options and **larger roles on the MPS platform**.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: MPS is an asset-light knowledge/technology business whose 'expansion' is acquisition-led rather than plant/capacity-led: management describes eleven acquisitions in thirteen years (since 2013), each integrated into a single operating engine rather than run as a separate business. In FY26 this took two concrete forms. First, MPS North America LLC completed the acquisition of a 100% equity stake in Unbound Medicine, Inc. (USA), a mobile-first, AI-enabled clinical decision-support and medical-education platform business, pursuant to a Stock Purchase Agreement dated 30 January 2026, marking MPS' entry into healthcare knowledge management. Second, MPS Interactive Systems Limited moved the Liberate Group (Liberate Learning Pty Ltd, Liberate eLearning Pty Ltd and App-eLearn Pty Ltd, Australia) from 65% to 100% ownership during the year, consolidating full control of the group and strengthening its Asia-Pacific corporate-learning presence; these entities, together with Liberate Learning, were subsequently unified under the single Liberate Global brand. No physical plant, capacity or manufacturing expansion is disclosed; the Company's stated estimated capital commitments outstanding as at 31 March 2026 were Nil, unchanged from the prior year.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Among the best-run calls in the batch. Structural choices that signal confidence: **six executives on the call**, with the two halves of Research narrated by the two people who actually run them and the Education head making his debut — *"Hearing about the business directly from the people building it is exactly how I want these calls to feel."* Substantively, management **quantified its own dilutions** (ex-AJE revenue and margin given unprompted), **corrected an analyst's misreading of the ₹1,500cr target** rather than letting a flattering error stand, **explicitly declined to promise Rule of 50 every quarter** (*"we are a conservative lot here at MPS when it comes to star gazing"*), **refused to commit Unbound synergy timelines** until the renewal cycle is understood, **conceded the organic-growth shortfall** when pushed (*"thank you for pushing us... The quarter that you see is in the rear-view mirror"*), and **disclosed a walked-away acquisition and its ethical reason**. The closing remarks summarised the analysts' three challenges back at them — including the demand for late-teens organic growth — which is unusual and credible. The only real gap: **no direct answer on why senior managers have been exiting**, beyond a general "the talent machine sometimes gets it wrong."

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Trusted content and proprietary workflows built over decades, with platforms customers run on daily
- AI engine applied selectively where it adds the most value, described as commercially tested against measurable value in customer workflows
- Deep, long-tenured customer relationships (some spanning twenty years) with expanding commitments, including an unprecedented five-year platform partnership and a first-for-industry volume commitment in research solutions in FY26
- Recognised for innovation in AI-driven research integrity and authenticity within the scholarly/STM domain
- Asset-light, people-and-technology business model with a deliberate delivery presence in Tier 2 Indian cities
- Balance sheet capacity to fund its own expansion (e.g. the Unbound Medicine acquisition) without straining capital

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **Organic growth is the acknowledged weak link.** Strip Unbound and group growth is **early-teens**; **Corporate Learning grows 6–7% into a 12–13% market**. The CEO accepted the challenge to reach late-teens but committed to no number or date.
2. **The AJE-offshoring cost offset is non-repeating.** It masked increments and Unbound headcount this quarter; from here, margin gains must come from mix and AI alone.
3. **Corporate Learning's margin jump is restructuring-led** (~33% headcount cut, largely a *"one-time reset"*). Holding 25.3% and progressing to 30% now requires the AI/immersive mix shift to actually land.
4. **Client count fell QoQ (906 → 841)** — explained entirely as AJE pruning, but worth verifying it stops now that management says *"the pruning is behind us."*
5. **Management churn** — an analyst opened by asking what is driving *"exits and replacements"* over the last year. The CEO's answer was candid but not reassuring: *"as the talent machine expands in a quick span of time, sometimes you make mistakes."* Education's business head was on his first MPS earnings call.
6. **Unbound is 18–20% margin against a 34% group margin** — near-term it is **dilutive to group margin** even as it is accretive to quality of revenue. The path to Rule of 40 is a target, not a plan.
7. **M&A dependency:** the FY28 ₹1,500cr/₹450cr target is difficult on early-teens organic growth alone, and deal timing is gated on *"a motivated seller"* — outside management's control.
8. **AJE reset must actually be over.** It has depressed reported Research and group growth for two years; a further leg down would undercut the *"grow on value rather than volume"* claim.
9. **Peer-review #1-by-year-end is a public, binary commitment** on a metric MPS does not control alone.
10. **Concentration in Research (55% of revenue at 45.1% margin)** — group margin is highly sensitive to any single-segment reversal.
11. **FX:** guidance assumes an unchanged planning rate; a sharp rupee appreciation would pressure a largely North-America-billed book.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The commoditisation argument is inverted, and coherently.** Most knowledge-services companies are AI-threatened because they sell generation. MPS argues that stronger models **increase** the value of verification, domain context and the workflow last mile. Whether or not it proves right, it is the correct axis on which to judge the business.
- **The moat is content *access rights*, not AI capability.** Unbound Intelligence's advantage is that it reads **behind publisher paywalls** — something no general model can replicate regardless of parameter count.
- **A 52% vs 32% manuscript acceptance rate is the quantitative licence to charge for outcomes.** This single statistic underwrites the entire pricing-model shift.
- **25% outcome-based and 45% recurring revenue** is now a stated portfolio characteristic *and* an acquisition screen — future deals are selected to preserve it.
- **Unbound: a 35-person team producing ~$9mn** with annual price increases on **every** renewal regardless of customer vintage. That pricing power, and the CEO's realisation that MPS has under-priced its own portfolio, may be the most valuable thing acquired.
- **Headcount flatness was an accounting coincidence, not a trend** — increments + Unbound were exactly offset by AJE offshoring. Do not extrapolate <3% headcount growth.
- **Offshoring that raised NPS.** *"I've never seen a transition like this where quality improves"* — attributed to greater operational control, and directly relevant to how future acquisitions will be integrated.
- **The FY28 bridge is arithmetically demanding:** from ~₹900cr annualised revenue to **₹1,500cr**, and from >₹300cr to **₹450cr** EBITDA, on early-teens organic growth. **Acquisitions are not optional to that target** — which is why the no-equity, ₹300–500cr, cash-plus-debt framework matters so much.
- **Distressed-asset ROCE was 30–50%+, and they gave it up anyway** — an unusually honest trade of financial accretion for management bandwidth.
- **"Rule of 50" is being used as an internal operating standard applied to acquisitions too** (Unbound → Rule of 40 → Rule of 50), not just as an investor-relations flourish.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Operate as an AI-first knowledge company organised around two capabilities, Discover (creation, validation and dissemination of knowledge) and Learn (delivery, application and assessment, now reaching the clinician at the point of care)
- Treat content, a publisher-grade platform, and AI capability as one compounding engine rather than separate services, with each asset making the others more valuable
- Expand into new adjacencies while carrying the existing footprint and relationships to them; entered healthcare knowledge management in FY26 through the acquisition of Unbound Medicine
- Embed AI …
